newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end near limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end near limit up.

text.p: CME lumber futures ran up from a lower start and closed near limit up on short covering, traders said.
Lumber closed $8.40 to $9.70 per tbf higher with November up $8.40 at $351.50 and January up $9.10 at $352.20 per tbf.
Initial carryover fund liquidation lacked follow through and prices turned up on short covering and speculative demand at a level some traders considered the potential bottom.

Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading, noted that the last time futures posted a sharp setback in June they fell $63 per tbf. When futures fell $63 from highs this time there was again buying interest in anticipation of a recovery.
"If you want to take a stand, I think these are the prices to at least nibble at with a stop loss someplace below it," Cunningham said.

The futures market had been anticipating a seasonal setback in cash prices and moved to a very sharp discount even before cash markets turned toppy. Cash prices will likely post a sharp setback in the next few weeks and narrow the gap they have with futures, traders added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce Wednesday at $430 per tbf, off $2.00 from both Friday and week-ago levels.
